plans.note: Section 9 is the express limitation of liability; check mutuality, cap size relative to fees paid by Corio, and carve-outs (indemnity in sec-8-2, confidentiality in sec-10).
Section 8 (INDEMNIFICATION) should carry Commerce One's IP infringement indemnity in favour of Corio; confirm any reciprocal Corio indemnity stays narrow and is not uncapped under sec-9.

Look for field-of-use or competitive-product restraints in the grant of rights (sec-3) and in defined terms CORIO MARKET SEGMENT / TERRITORY (sec-1-2); shared resources (sec-13) may also restrict Corio's other offerings.

Check whether the grant or the CORIO MARKET SEGMENT definition obliges Corio to host only Commerce One software or to source procurement functionality exclusively; Exhibit D sales/marketing cooperation may add soft exclusivity.

Pricing, revenue-sharing and payment terms are the only plausible home for a most-favoured-pricing clause; flag only if it obliges Corio to give Commerce One best terms, and welcome any MFN running to Corio.
No dedicated personnel clause in the outline; if a non-solicit exists it would sit in Miscellaneous (sec-14) or alongside shared resources/personnel (sec-13). Confirm before marking missing.

Section 11 governs term and termination; test whether Corio has convenience termination on notice without penalty and whether Commerce One holds any unilateral mid-term exit or fee acceleration (cross-check sec-4/sec-17).
Initial term, renewal terms and notice window will be in sec-11; check renewal pricing uplift against Exhibit B pricing.
Governing law, venue and any arbitration (note the defined term RULES, suggesting arbitral rules) should appear in Miscellaneous; verify forum is a court in an accepted jurisdiction.

Assignment/change-of-control language is normally in sec-14; check whether Commerce One may terminate on a Corio change of control (cross-reference sec-11) and whether Corio may assign to affiliates and successors.

Ownership turns on the grant of rights (sec-3) and the DEVELOPMENTS / EMPLOYEE NDA-INVENTION AGREEMENT definitions (sec-1-2); confirm Corio retains its own IP, customer data and any Corio-developed work, and check trademark licence scope in sec-6.

Section 2 (sec-3) is the licence grant; test scope for Corio affiliates, contractors and CUSTOMER(S)/SOFTWARE USER access, territory limits, and that the grant is not revocable at will. Delivery terms in sec-3-2 and Exhibit A (sec-1-3, sec-2).

A records/audit right against Corio most likely accompanies the revenue-sharing and payment terms (Exhibit B, sec-17/sec-p0155) or sits in Miscellaneous; check notice, frequency, business-hours limits and who bears cost.
Look for late-payment interest, penalties or minimum shortfall payments in fees/payment terms; service credits running to Corio (support in sec-5, Exhibit C) are acceptable and should not be flagged.

Section 7 (sec-8) holds the warranties and disclaimer; check the Warranty Period and Acceptance Test definitions (sec-1-2) and whether the remedy is meaningful beyond repair-or-refund, supported by maintenance in sec-5 and Exhibit C.
No insurance heading appears in the outline; sweep Miscellaneous and the indemnification section before concluding it is missing.
Exhibit B pricing and revenue-sharing fees are the likely source of minimum guarantees or committed licence volumes on Corio; check for any exit or true-up relief in sec-11.
Effects-of-termination wind-down should be in sec-11; source code escrow (sec-12) partially covers continuity but confirm data return and migration assistance for Corio and its CUSTOMER(S).
